questions: With the sensor row at y = 0.07 m, does the robot still leave the line early, and at what progress and curvature?
Does steering_oscillation rise on the slalom compared with iteration 1 (lead 0.05 m)? If so, is the lead overshooting?
Does the 15 mm spacing still give a clean monotonic signal, or do outer sensors drop out at the larger errors seen near the limit?
Is the failure now limited by controller gain or base speed rather than sensing? State which, so I know whether to keep changing geometry.
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If lead 0.07 m overshoots on the slalom, suggest a value between 0.05 and 0.07 m. If the s-bend still fails at the same progress, state whether sensor spacing or wheel_radius should change next.

intent: Test whether more forward sensor lead (y 0.05 to 0.07 m) reduces the early off-track departures that persisted through iterations 0 and 1. Only the sensor lead changes, so the effect is isolated from drivetrain. Expected result: max_error below 0.05 m, more progress on the oval and s-bend, and no large rise in slalom oscillation.
learning: Iterations 0 and 1 show that the 0.06 m off-track limit is fixed by the floor, and that drivetrain changes give only marginal, track-dependent gains (oval down, s-bend up). The remaining untested geometry lever is sensor forward lead. This iteration tests it alone. Measurements to watch: max_error, rms_error, progress, steering_oscillation and line_loss_events on all three development tracks.
rationale: Evidence: in both iterations every development run ended off track at 11-16% progress. Max error sits at 0.06-0.07 m, just past the off-track limit. With body_width 0.12 the limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.03) = 0.06 m. Iteration 1 (track 0.12 to 0.10 m, mass 0.8 to 0.6 kg) raised the score only from 52.18 to 52.33. It helped the s-bend (65.8 vs 64.1) and slightly hurt the oval (45.9 vs 47.3), and runs still left the line. Body width cannot change the limit, since 0.18 m still gives the 0.06 m floor, so the robot must hold its error below 0.06 m. Drivetrain changes gave only small gains, which points to the sensing lead as the next lever. The current row is at y = 0.05 m, so the sensors see the line only about 0.05 m ahead of the axle. At speed the correction arrives late on curves. This iteration changes one thing: sensor forward position from y = 0.05 to y = 0.07 m, a 20 mm gain in lead, within the 0.08 m limit. Track 0.10 m, mass 0.6 kg, wheel radius 0.03 m, body 0.18 x 0.12 m and the 12 mm sensors at 15 mm spacing stay the same, so any change can be attributed to the lead. Expected result: the robot sees the upcoming bend earlier, so max_error falls below about 0.05 m and progress rises on the oval and slalom. Risk: a longer lead can overshoot and increase steering oscillation on the slalom. If that happens, the next step is to shorten the lead or reduce spacing, not to change the body.
